workload.note: embedding model: prefill+norm+mean-pool only, no decode/LM-head/sampling

roofline_basis: 3.72 TFLOP matmul (all 5 roles BFP4/LoFi) / 580.9 TFLOPS measured P150 BFP4-LoFi peak (tech_reports/GEMM_FLOPS)
named_limitations: bs>=8 MinimalMatmul rows were SLOW at 48% of BFP4/LoFi peak because subblock_h/subblock_w were left at the binding default of 1; 1x8 fixes the bound classification. Re-profile to confirm the new FLOPs% before treating batched matmul as exhausted.
subblock is capped by DST: 2x8 fails 'subblock_h * subblock_w must be <= max_dest_volume', so 1x8 already uses the whole 8-tile budget

bs>=8 still runs dram_interleaved end to end: a bs32 activation is 41.9 MB. TT_BATCHED_L1_PREFILL with caps of 24/32 MB and MM blocks shrunk to 4,4,4 / 4,8,8 / 6,8,8 all fail with 'statically allocated dataflow buffers clash with L1 buffer'
legacy MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast rejected for batch (bs8 220.2 vs 189.3, bs32 868.9 vs 707.2 ms) while it is correct at bs=1 (33.1 vs 49.0 ms)
MLP prefill chunking rejected: bs32 705.8 -> 746.1 (chunk 4096) -> 780.7 ms (2048)
bs=1 matmuls are FLOP-bound at 69-70% of peak and unaffected by subblock (legacy path derives out_subblock_w itself); its remaining 45% is SDPA/LayerNorm/BinaryNg/Rotary
device is harvested 120/130 cores, so absolute numbers are ~8% pessimistic vs a full P150
